title: A task over its budget keeps its work: the overrun is its own record, not a gate abort; the next task continues its branch and is told so; a second overrun goes to the supervisor
prompt:
Read, in crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs, the module comment (the halt rules, budgets), `HALT_AFTER`, `halt_reason`, `over_budget` and `enforce_budget` (the Stop, then `{"type": "task.aborted", "id", "reason"}`); `tool_calls_since` in crates/spawn-postgres (the `tool.started` events of the task's session after its delivery); in crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql the fold of `task.aborted` in `spawn_control_apply` ("Over budget: the work is dropped, and it counts toward the abort halt": state cancelled, gate_aborts + 1), `spawn_integrator_record` (the record types the integrator may write, and the states each needs) and `spawn_objective_assign` (resident or a new per-task worker `agent_worker_objective_<task>`); crates/spawn-cli/src/objectives.rs (`assign_next`, `choose`, `brief`, `assign`); crates/spawn-cli/src/deliver.rs's module comment (a Stop takes a final checkpoint; a cancelled resident's work set aside and its notice) and crates/spawn-cli/src/set_aside.rs; crates/spawn-cli/src/push.rs (each branch pushed to the source's `spawn/<agent>` at most once per 5 s, after its checkpoint); the start of a per-task worker's workspace (from the source's main) in the Bridge and crates/spawn-host; the dispatcher's escalations in crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch.rs (`Why`, `Escalation`, the host items, and `gate_room_escalations` in crates/spawn-cli/src/disk.rs, an integrator record that reaches the supervisor once, tagged `host gate-room-<event id>`); docs/fleet-architecture.md §3 and §10.4 and docs/design.md §14.

The problem. On 2026-11-06 mission 4's task 84 (objective 017), on agent_worker_objective_84, hit the mission's 150 tool-call budget 51 minutes after its delivery. The integrator stopped it and recorded `task.aborted` ("the task made more than 150 tool calls") at 05:12:59 UTC, which the mission counts as a gate abort (three in a row halt it), and six seconds later issued objective 017 again as task 87 on a fresh agent_worker_objective_87, from main, whose brief said nothing of task 84. Task 84's branch spawn/agent_worker_objective_84 held 4,259 lines in 21 files (head d44c601) of 51 minutes of model work; task 87 started over from nothing and would have hit the same budget at the same point, three times, then halted the mission. A budget overrun is not a failed gate and says nothing about the host or the work's quality: it says the task is bigger than its budget. The owner's goal (2026-11-06) is the Pareto frontier: no dimension improves by letting another regress; this loses work (cost, lead time) and halts missions (autonomy, reliability) for nothing.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks).
1. An overrun is its own record. A delivered task over its mission's budget is stopped as today (the Stop and its final checkpoint) and recorded `{"type": "task.over_budget", "id", "reason", "tool_calls", "elapsed_ms", "budget"}` (budget: the mission's, as it was), not `task.aborted`. It counts toward no halt: gate_aborts and gate_rejections stay as they were, and no run of either is broken or started by it. The task leaves flight (it frees its slot) and is not reported or gated. `task.aborted` keeps its other meaning (a landing gone stale after its mission was done).
2. The objective's next task continues it. The next task of the objective after an overrun is assigned only once the overrun task's work has reached its branch: its Stop ended with its final checkpoint, and the source's spawn/<agent> holds that checkpoint (the pusher's head), or the branch's push failed, which is said in the log and the brief. Its `task.assigned` names `continues` (the overrun task's id). Its workspace starts from that branch's head, not from main: on a new per-task worker, the workspace is made from that commit (the source's main merged in, as a live worker's is before a task); or on the overrun task's own agent, resumed. What its worker is told names the overrun task (#id, its objective, the reason and the tool calls), the branch (spawn/<agent>), the commit (its id, 7 or more hex digits) and that commit's diff stat against main (`git diff --stat main <commit>`: the per-file lines and the summary line), and says the work is in its workspace to continue, not to redo. The budget of the continuing task is the mission's; it may be raised once, for that task only, to at most twice the budget (say so in the record and the brief).
3. A second overrun goes to the supervisor. An overrun of a task that continues an overrun task of the same objective is recorded as in (1) and escalated to the supervisor once: a digest item tagged `host over-budget-<event id of its record>`, naming both tasks (#id each), the objective, the branch and its diff stat, the budget and the tool calls, and what can be done (split the objective, raise the budget with `spawn mission configure`, or take it over). The objective is then held: no task is issued for it until the mission is configured again (a `mission.configured` record newer than the escalated overrun's record). The mission's other objectives go on: the freed slot goes to the next open objective. A third overrun, after such a configure, is treated as a first.
4. Causality (§14): a continuation names what it continues (the task, the branch, the commit) in its own record and its brief, and the commit is read from the source after the Stop's final checkpoint reached it, never assumed; a hold is decided from records (the two overruns, the newest `mission.configured`), never from memory of the integrator's process.

How the saving shows, in numbers. Task 84's 51 minutes of work (4,259 lines, 21 files) would have been continued by task 87 instead of redone. Of mission 4's 22 tasks so far two overran, both recorded as gate aborts with their work dropped: task 22 (objective 006, past its 45-minute budget, 2026-11-05 12:09 UTC) and task 84. On 017's scorecard: cost (model tokens per landed objective) and lead time fall by the redone work; reliability no worse and autonomy higher: an overrun is no abort, so no halt for a human to resume (today three overruns of one objective halt the mission, which the scenario shows in 15-29 s). Rework no longer counts a re-issue that starts over.

State the rule in integrate.rs's module comment (budgets: the overrun, the continuation, the escalation and the hold), in objectives.rs's module comment, in docs/fleet-architecture.md §10.4 and in schema.sql beside the fold. Add unit tests: `over_budget` unchanged; an overrun is recorded `task.over_budget` and changes neither gate_aborts nor gate_rejections; three overruns halt nothing; the next task of the objective carries `continues` and is assigned only once the branch holds the final checkpoint; its brief names the task, the branch, the commit and the diff stat; a second overrun in a chain escalates once and holds the objective; a `mission.configured` after it releases the hold; the next open objective takes the freed slot. In crates/spawn-postgres/tests/: the fold of `task.over_budget` (the task out of flight, no counter moved) and `spawn_integrator_record` accepting it only for a delivered task.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/026.sh (read it: its header lists today's measures). A real `spawn loop` (the Bridge, its pusher, the dispatcher, the supervisor, no model judge) runs every agent on a fake engine, and `spawn integrate --once` passes, run by the scenario, enforce the budget and assign objectives. One gated objective mission (accept gate, a budget of 5 tool calls, 2 workers) whose resident `keeper` holds a task of the mission, so objective tasks go to per-task workers as task 84 did. Objective 961's engine notes whether big.txt is in its workspace (and its sha256), writes it (120 lines) if not, then makes a tool call every 0.2 s until stopped; objective 962's writes a file and makes none. It checks:
- (1) T1 (961) goes past 5 tool calls: within 45 s of its delivery a record for it says so; it is `task.over_budget` with `reason`, `tool_calls` (more than 5) and `budget` ({"tool_calls": 5}); no `task.aborted`; gate_aborts and gate_rejections stay 0;
- (2) within 60 s of that record T2 (961) is assigned with `continues` T1; the text delivered to its worker names T1's branch, a commit of it (7+ hex) whose tree holds T1's big.txt, and that commit's diff stat against main (the `--shortstat` line and big.txt); T2's engine finds big.txt in its workspace, the bytes of that commit's;
- (3) T2 goes past the budget too: within 60 s of its delivery a `task.over_budget` record (no `task.aborted`); within 40 s of it a digest delivered to the supervisor names #T1 and #T2, and objective 962 gets a task; after five more integrator passes objective 961 has exactly those two tasks, the supervisor was told once, gate_aborts is 0 and the mission is not halted.
On the live main (49b92be; the deployed binary is built from it) it fails at (1): "(1) task #2's budget overrun was recorded as task.aborted (the task made more than 5 tool calls), a gate abort: the mission's gate_aborts went from 0 to 1, toward the halt after three; an overrun is a record of its own (task.over_budget) and counts toward no halt". With BB_026_MEASURE=1 (only to show today's behaviour) it goes on: T1 aborted 2.43-2.53 s after its delivery; T2 assigned 137-157 ms later on a fresh worker, with no `continues`, told nothing of T1, finding no big.txt although T1's branch holds it (1 file changed, 120 insertions(+)) by the time T2 starts (the Stop's final checkpoint reaches the source after the abort's record: a continuation must wait for it); T2 aborted, a third task for 961, the mission halted "3 gate aborts in a row", the supervisor told nothing and 962 never assigned. It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, a new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]) and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
